sections.h2: What does the DeKalb County Clerk of Superior Court do when a house sells?
sections.html:
The clerk's Real Estate Division records the deed that moves title from seller to buyer, along with mortgages, plats, liens and other papers that touch land in DeKalb County. The office says it receives more than 204,500 real estate documents a year, and its records run back to 1842 because earlier books burned in a fire.

The clerk's FAQ describes three roles: clerk of court, registrar of land records, and collector of intangible and transfer taxes. For a seller that means one counter handles the recording, the transfer tax certification and the public index that a title examiner searches before closing.

The Census Bureau counts 267.74 land square miles in DeKalb and estimated 774,394 residents for 2025. The county seat is Decatur.

sections.h2: Where is the Real Estate Division and when is it open?
sections.html:
The division is on the ground floor at 556 N. McDonough Street, Decatur, GA 30030. The real estate page lists 404-687-3812 and weekday hours from half past eight in the morning until five in the afternoon The clerk's general information line is 404-371-2836.

Property records are searchable online through the county's deed search and in the public access room. Searches go fastest when you have three facts in hand:

  • The buyer's name (grantee) and the seller's name (grantor)
  • The year of the transaction
  • The tax parcel ID, which every conveyance filed here must now carry

Copies by mail need the book type and page number, and the office will not process a request without them. Pay by cashier's check, money order or attorney's check made out to the DeKalb County Clerk of Court. Certified copies can also be ordered through the eCertification portal, where an approved request must be paid within six days or it is rejected automatically.

  • Certified copy: $2.50 for the first page, 50 cents for each added page
  • Regular copy: $1.00 per page
  • Plat copy: $2.00 per page
  • Card payments on the fee chart page carry a surcharge of 2% plus $1.00

sections.h2: Can a seller still bring a deed to the DeKalb clerk's counter or mail it?
sections.html:
No. Since January 1, 2025, Georgia House Bill 1292 requires every real estate document in DeKalb County to be filed electronically, and mail-in recording is closed to new filings. The clerk accepts e-recordings from approved providers listed on its page, including Simplifile and CSC.

Anyone who is a party to the instrument and files on their own must also upload a government-issued ID at efile.gsccca.org, where it is verified before the filing can go through. The page cites O.C.G.A. 44-2-39(b)(1) for that step. Most sellers never touch this step, since the firm running the closing e-records the deed. If you are selling without an attorney, such as a family transfer, build the ID check into your timeline.

Plats follow the same electronic rule and have been e-file only since 2017, and UCC financing statements became e-file only in 2022.

sections.h2: What has to be in the package before the clerk will record a deed?
sections.html:
Every deed of conveyance needs a PT-61 transfer tax form and the tax parcel ID printed at the top of its first page. Georgia has required that parcel ID on DeKalb transfers and conveyances since July 1, 2019, under House Bill 694.

The PT-61 is completed online at the Georgia Superior Court Clerks' Cooperative Authority site, printed, and submitted with the deed. The clerk does not supply forms, the document must be complete before it arrives, and most documents need a signature, a witness and a notary. State identification is required for any filing.

One point sellers like: original documents are recorded immediately and handed back, a rule the clerk cites as O.C.G.A. 15-6-72. The recording fee schedule is posted on the clerk's fee page as a Real Estate Fees chart. Ask the clerk or your closing attorney for the current figure rather than relying on an older number, because Georgia moved to flat filing fees in 2020 under House Bill 288.

sections.h2: How much is the Georgia transfer tax and who pays it?
sections.html:
The seller owes it by law, though a sales contract often shifts it to the buyer. The Georgia Department of Revenue prints the rate as $1 for the first $1,000 of the sale price, plus 10 cents for each additional $100 or fraction of $100.

Payment comes first; the clerk then attaches a certification that it has been paid. The governing statutes are O.C.G.A. 48-6-1 through 48-6-10. For questions about exemptions, the Department of Revenue points people to the clerk of superior court in the county.

A separate intangible recording tax applies to a long-term note secured by real estate. The Department of Revenue lists it at $1.50 for each $500 of the note's face amount, and the clerk collects it in DeKalb County. A payoff and release on your existing loan is a cancellation of the security deed, and the clerk's page says more than 26,500 mortgages are cancelled in the county each year.

sections.h2: What recording deadlines and rules apply to DeKalb County documents?
sections.html:
Several documents carry a clock that starts when they are signed or when work ends. The clerk's real estate page lists the ones below.

DocumentRule on the clerk's pageAuthority cited
Deed of conveyancePT-61 and parcel ID required; transfer tax due at recordingO.C.G.A. 48-6-1, 48-6-2
Security deedDue 90 days after signing, or penalty and interest on intangible tax when the maturity is over three yearsO.C.G.A. 48-6-61
Foreclosure deedFile within 120 days of signing to avoid a $500 penaltyStated on the clerk's page
Materialmen's or laborer's lienFile within 90 days of the last work or materials; it expires 395 days after filing without a lawsuitO.C.G.A. 44-14-361, 44-14-367
Bond to discharge a lienClerk must approve the bond before it is recordedO.C.G.A. 44-14-364

Table source: DeKalb County Clerk of Superior Court, Real Estate page.

sections.h2: How can a DeKalb homeowner guard against a fraudulent filing?
sections.html:
The clerk participates in the Filing Activity Notification System, called FANS, run through the Georgia clerks' authority at fans.gsccca.org. A homeowner registers a property, or the properties of family members, and gets an email when a deed, lien or similar paper is filed or indexed against it. Owners who signed up under the older DeKalb alert system had to register again for FANS.

This matters before a sale because a forged deed or a surprise lien surfaces in the title search and can stall a closing. If you inherit a house or hold one that sits vacant, an alert is cheap protection. A veteran can also record a DD-214 discharge with the clerk at no charge, which keeps a certified copy on file locally.

sections.h2: What does DeKalb County's housing market look like for a seller?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau's QuickFacts table lists 337,059 housing units in DeKalb County in 2025 and 58.8% owner-occupancy for 2020 to 2024. Homes that owners live in had a middle value of $357,800, tenants paid $1,692 in median gross rent, and 1,321 building permits were issued in 2025.

  • Median household income: $80,644 (2020 to 2024, in 2024 dollars)
  • Mean commute: 30.4 minutes
  • Bachelor's degree or higher among adults 25 and over: 47.4%
  • Foreign-born residents: 17.3%

DeKalb was formed in 1822 and lost its western half to Fulton County in 1853. Interstates 20, 85, 285 and 675 cross it, and MARTA rail serves the east and northeast lines. A house in unincorporated DeKalb, in Decatur, in Brookhaven or in Stonecrest all record at the same clerk's office, even though each sits under a different city government.

faqs.q: Do I have to go to Decatur to file my deed?
faqs.a: No. Real estate documents in DeKalb County must be filed electronically, and self-filers upload a government ID at efile.gsccca.org first. The closing firm usually e-records for a sale.

faqs.q: Who pays the Georgia transfer tax on a home sale?
faqs.a: The seller is liable under Georgia law, though the contract can assign it to the buyer. The Department of Revenue rate is $1 for the first $1,000 and 10 cents per added $100 or fraction of $100, paid before recording.

faqs.q: When must a security deed or foreclosure deed be recorded?
faqs.a: A security deed should be filed within 90 days of signing, and a foreclosure deed within 120 days, which the clerk's page ties to a $500 penalty if missed. Check dates with the closing attorney.

faqs.q: How do I get a certified copy of a recorded deed?
faqs.a: Use the eCertification portal or mail a request with the book type and page number. The clerk lists certified copies at $2.50 for page one and 50 cents for each added page, and an approved portal order must be paid within six days.

faqs.q: What is a PT-61 and why does the clerk require it?
faqs.a: It is Georgia's real estate transfer tax declaration, completed online and printed. Every deed of conveyance in DeKalb County must carry one, plus the tax parcel ID on page one, before the clerk can record it.
